children.title: Strong Convexity
children.top_down_role: Uniform quadratic lower curvature and its primal, differential, operator, and dual views.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, and let \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real-valued Hilbert-space definition with curvature measured by the Hilbert norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex if \(\operatorname{dom}f\) is convex and, for all \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(\theta\in[0,1]\), \[f(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)\le\theta f(x)+(1-\theta)f(y)-\frac\mu2\theta(1-\theta)\|x-y\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper function is strongly convex with parameter mu when its Jensen inequality contains a uniform quadratic deficit proportional to the squared distance between the endpoints. The parameter depends on the ambient norm and measures uniform lower curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f)(\forall\theta\in[0,1])\;f(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)\le\theta f(x)+(1-\theta)f(y)-\frac\mu2\theta(1-\theta)\|x-y\|^2.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(f-\frac\mu2\|\cdot\|^2\) is convex.
If \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, then \(f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac\mu2\|y-x\|^2\) for every \(g\in\partial f(x)\).
Under the same closed convex hypotheses, \(\partial f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone.
special_cases_latex: The quadratic \(x\mapsto\frac12\langle Ax,x\rangle+b^Tx+c\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex exactly when \(A\succeq\mu I\).
Strong convexity is uniform convexity with modulus \(t\mapsto\frac\mu2t^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A proper closed strongly convex function has at most one minimizer and, on the whole Hilbert space, has a unique minimizer.
At a minimizer \(x^*\), \(f(x)-f(x^*)\ge\frac\mu2\|x-x^*\|^2\).
boundary_notes: Strict convexity alone does not supply a positive strong-convexity parameter.
Changing the norm changes the admissible value of \(\mu\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Convexity via Quadratic Subgradient Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines strong convexity in Euclidean space and records its shifted-convexity and quadratic-lower-model characterizations. Complexity claims are excluded because the extract does not state their full oracle-class assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be convex and let \(\alpha\ge 0\). A function \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is \(\alpha\)-strongly convex if, for all \(x,y\in\mathcal X\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\), \[f(y)\ge f(x)+g^\top(y-x)+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] Equivalently, \(x\mapsto f(x)-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|x\|^2\) is convex. Thus \(q^-_{x,g}(y)=f(x)+g^\top(y-x)+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|y-x\|^2\) is a touching quadratic lower bound for \(f\). If \(f\) is twice differentiable, strong convexity implies \(\nabla^2 f(x)\succeq\alpha I\) wherever the Hessian is defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is alpha-strongly convex when every subgradient affine lower bound can be strengthened by an alpha-quadratic term. Equivalently, subtracting alpha times the squared norm divided by two leaves a convex function. Each subgradient therefore defines a touching quadratic lower model. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral characterization and maximal strong-convexity modulus for finite-dimensional quadratics under the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbb R^n\) be endowed with the \(\ell_2\)-norm and let
\[
f(x)=\frac12x^TAx+b^Tx+c,
\qquad A\in\mathbb S^n,\quad b\in\mathbb R^n,\quad c\in\mathbb R.
\]
For \(\sigma>0\), \(f\) is \(\sigma\)-strongly convex if and only if
\[
A-\sigma I\succeq0,
\]
equivalently, if and only if \(\lambda_{\min}(A)\geq\sigma\). Consequently, \(f\) is strongly convex if and only if \(A\succ0\); when this holds, its largest possible strong-convexity parameter is \(\lambda_{\min}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic with symmetric matrix A is sigma-strongly convex exactly when A minus sigma times the identity is positive semidefinite, equivalently when the smallest eigenvalue of A is at least sigma. It is strongly convex exactly when A is positive definite, and then its largest admissible parameter is the smallest eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is }\sigma\text{-strongly convex}\iff A-\sigma I\succeq0\iff\lambda_{\min}(A)\geq\sigma;\quad f\text{ is strongly convex}\iff A\succ0,\quad \sigma_{\max}=\lambda_{\min}(A).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Convexity via a Quadratic Subgradient Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition preserving the source's pairwise existential subgradient quantifier; this quantifier should not be silently replaced by the more common arbitrary-subgradient formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \hat\sigma>0. The function \hat f is strongly convex with parameter \hat\sigma if, for every x,y\in\operatorname{dom}\hat f, there exists g\in\partial\hat f(x) such that
\[
\hat f(y)\ge \hat f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{\hat\sigma}{2}\|y-x\|^2.
\]
If \hat f is differentiable, the source states that this is equivalent to
\[
\hat f(y)\ge \hat f(x)+\langle\nabla\hat f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\hat\sigma}{2}\|y-x\|^2\qquad\forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}\hat f.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity with parameter hat-sigma is defined by a quadratic lower bound: for each pair of domain points, the source requires some subgradient at the first point that supports the bound. In the differentiable case, it gives the corresponding gradient inequality for every pair of points.
assumptions_latex: \hat f\text{ is defined on a normed domain}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}\hat f\;\exists g\in\partial\hat f(x):\quad \hat f(y)\ge \hat f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{\hat\sigma}{2}\|y-x\|^2,\quad\text{with the stated gradient equivalent if }\hat f\text{ is differentiable.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex if and only if its Fenchel conjugate
\[
f^*(u)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{\langle u,x\rangle-f(x)\}
\]
is differentiable on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) and satisfies
\[
\|\nabla f^*(u)-\nabla f^*(v)\|_2\le\frac{1}{\mu}\|u-v\|_2
\quad\text{for all }u,v\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
The reciprocal constant \(1/\mu\) is the conjugate smoothness modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed convex f is mu-strongly convex exactly when its conjugate is differentiable with a 1/mu-Lipschitz gradient.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\sigma>0\). The following are equivalent: (a) \(f^*\) is strongly convex with modulus \(\sigma\); (b) \(f\) is differentiable and \(\nabla f\) is globally Lipschitz with constant \(1/\sigma\); (c) whenever \(v_i\in\partial f(x_i)\), \[\langle v_1-v_0,x_1-x_0\rangle\geq\sigma\|v_1-v_0\|^2;\] (d) \(f=f_0\mathbin{\oplus}\frac{1}{2\sigma}\|\cdot\|^2\) for some convex function \(f_0\); and (e) \(f\) is differentiable and \[f(x')\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),x'-x\rangle+\frac{1}{2\sigma}\|x'-x\|^2\quad\forall x,x'\in\mathbb{R}^n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function, strong convexity of its conjugate with modulus sigma is equivalent to differentiability and one-over-sigma Lipschitz continuity of the primal gradient, inverse strong monotonicity of the subdifferential, an infimal-convolution representation with a quadratic, and a global quadratic upper model.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, and let \(\phi:\mathbb R_+\to[0,+\infty]\) be increasing and vanish only at \(0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real-valued Hilbert-space uniform convexity, including nonquadratic moduli and power-type subclasses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is uniformly convex with modulus \(\phi\) if, for all \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(\theta\in(0,1)\), \[f(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)+\theta(1-\theta)\phi(\|x-y\|)\le\theta f(x)+(1-\theta)f(y).\] It is uniformly convex if it admits at least one such modulus. A power-type modulus has the form \(\phi(t)=c t^p\) with \(c>0\) and an admissible exponent \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform convexity strengthens strict convexity by requiring a Jensen deficit controlled solely by the distance between the two endpoints. The controlling function is the modulus of convexity and need not be quadratic. Strong convexity is the quadratic special case.
assumptions_latex: The inequality is required for all domain points and all \(0<\theta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f)(\forall\theta\in(0,1))\;f(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)+\theta(1-\theta)\phi(\|x-y\|)\le\theta f(x)+(1-\theta)f(y).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The exact modulus is the pointwise infimum of the normalized Jensen deficit over pairs at a prescribed distance and mixing parameters.
Uniform convexity holds exactly when the exact modulus vanishes only at \(0\).
special_cases_latex: Strong convexity with constant \(\mu\) corresponds to \(\phi(t)=\frac\mu2t^2\).
Functions such as \(\|\cdot\|^p\) for \(p\ge2\) provide standard nonquadratic uniformly convex examples.
immediate_consequences_latex: Uniform convexity implies strict convexity.
If \(f\) is proper and convex, uniform convexity of \(f\) with modulus \(\phi\) makes \(\partial f\) uniformly monotone with modulus \(2\phi\).
boundary_notes: Strict convexity need not be uniform on an unbounded domain.
The modulus and power-type constants depend on the norm and on whether the property is global or restricted to a subset.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform convexity with a modulus and strong convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global and subset-restricted definitions for proper extended-real-valued functions on a Hilbert space, including the associated convexity hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, and let \(\phi:\mathbb R_+\to[0,+\infty]\) be increasing and vanish only at \(0\). Then \(f\) is uniformly convex with modulus \(\phi\) if, for every \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)+\alpha(1-\alpha)\phi(\|x-y\|)\leq \alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y).
\]
It is strongly convex with constant \(\beta>0\) when this inequality holds with \(\phi(t)=\frac{\beta}{2}t^2\). For a nonempty \(C\subset\operatorname{dom}f\), uniform convexity on \(C\) is defined by the same inequality restricted to \(x,y\in C\). Moreover,
\[
\text{strong convexity}\Rightarrow\text{uniform convexity}\Rightarrow\text{strict convexity}\Rightarrow\text{convexity},
\]
and none of these implications is reversible in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform convexity requires every nontrivial convex combination to gain a distance-dependent amount of curvature. The same condition restricted to endpoints in a nonempty subset defines uniform convexity on that subset. A positive quadratic modulus gives strong convexity. Strong convexity implies uniform convexity, which implies strict convexity, which implies convexity, and none of these implications reverses in general.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)+\alpha(1-\alpha)\phi(\|x-y\|)\leq\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y),\quad \phi(t)=\tfrac{\beta}{2}t^2\text{ in the strongly convex case}

Let \(g:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R_+\) be uniformly convex with exact modulus of convexity \(\varphi\), and let \(p\in[1,+\infty)\). Then \(g^p\) is uniformly convex, and its exact modulus of convexity \(\chi\) satisfies
\[
\chi\ge 2^{1-2p}\min\{p2^{1-p},1-2^{-p}\}\,\varphi^p.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a nonnegative-valued function on a Hilbert space is uniformly convex with exact modulus φ, then its p-th power is uniformly convex for every p at least 1. The exact modulus χ has the stated lower bound in terms of φ.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R_+\) is uniformly convex with exact modulus of convexity \(\varphi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g^p\) is uniformly convex, and its exact modulus \(\chi\) satisfies \(\chi\ge 2^{1-2p}\min\{p2^{1-p},1-2^{-p}\}\varphi^p\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is uniformly convex of power type \(p\) with constant \(c\) when, for all \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(t\in[0,1]\),
\[
f((1-t)x+ty)
\le(1-t)f(x)+tf(y)-c\,t(1-t)\|x-y\|^p.
\]
This is modulus-based uniform convexity with \(\phi(r)=cr^p\). The case \(p=2\) recovers quadratic uniform curvature up to the chosen normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power-type uniform convexity uses a Jensen-gap modulus equal to a positive constant times the p-th power of distance.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), a global deficit \(c\,t(1-t)|x-y|^p\) with \(c>0\) exists exactly when \(p=2\). It fails for \(1<p<2\) at arbitrarily small separations and for \(p>2\) at arbitrarily large separations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the whole real line, quadratic strong convexity is not power-type uniform convexity with an exponent other than two.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Power Growth of Subgradients and Objective Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constants use the accepted seed's Jensen-gap normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) is uniformly convex of power type \(p\) with constant \(c\), then
\[
f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle+c\|y-x\|^p
\quad(s\in\partial f(x)),
\]
and
\[
\langle s-r,x-y\rangle\ge2c\|x-y\|^p
\quad(s\in\partial f(x),\ r\in\partial f(y)).
\]
Every global minimizer \(x_*\) satisfies
\[
f(x)-f(x_*)\ge c\|x-x_*\|^p.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power-type uniform convexity yields p-order subgradient growth and a p-order objective-error bound around a global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) satisfies the accepted seed with \(\phi(r)=cr^p\), where \(c>0\) and \(p>1\).
The displayed subgradients exist at the relevant points.
\(x_*\) is a global minimizer when the objective-error assertion is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle s-r,x-y\rangle\ge2c\|x-y\|^p\), and \(f(x)-f(x_*)\ge c\|x-x_*\|^p\).
knowledge_statements.title: Power Growth of Subgradients and Objective Error

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), the Jensen gap is \(\tfrac12t(1-t)|x-y|^2\). Therefore an inequality with deficit \(c\,t(1-t)|x-y|^p\) for all \(x,y\) and some \(c>0\) can hold only for \(p=2\): for \(1<p<2\) it fails as \(|x-y|\to0\), and for \(p>2\) it fails as \(|x-y|\to\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient-Difference Upper Bound for the Bregman Remainder
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An upper bound on an oriented first-order remainder under power-type uniform convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb{E}$ be convex, let $p\ge 2$, and let $d:Q\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable and uniformly convex on $Q$ of degree $p$ with parameter $\sigma_p>0$. Then, for every $x,y\in Q$,
\[
d(y)-d(x)-\langle\nabla d(x),y-x\rangle
\le \frac{p-1}{p}\,\sigma_p^{-1/(p-1)}\|\nabla d(y)-\nabla d(x)\|_*^{p/(p-1)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a differentiable function uniformly convex of degree p, the first-order remainder from x to y is bounded above by (p−1)/p times sigma_p to the power −1/(p−1), multiplied by the dual-norm gradient difference raised to p/(p−1).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient Uniform Monotonicity Implies Power-Type Uniform Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient condition for power-type uniform convexity of a differentiable function on a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $Q$ be closed and convex and let $d:Q\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable. Suppose that for some $p\ge 2$ and $\sigma>0$,
\[
\langle\nabla d(x)-\nabla d(y),x-y\rangle\ge \sigma\|x-y\|^p,\qquad \forall x,y\in Q.
\]
Then $d$ is uniformly convex on $Q$ of degree $p$ with parameter $\sigma$; that is,
\[
d(y)\ge d(x)+\langle\nabla d(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\sigma}{p}\|y-x\|^p,\qquad \forall x,y\in Q.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the gradient of a differentiable function on a closed convex set is uniformly monotone with p-power modulus sigma, then the function is uniformly convex of degree p with the same parameter sigma.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x,y\in Q,\quad d(y)\ge d(x)+\langle\nabla d(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\sigma}{p}\|y-x\|^p

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional normed space with dual \(X^*\).
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(\phi\) is proper, convex, nondecreasing, supercoercive, and satisfies \(\phi(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The \(\phi\)-curvature inequality for \(f\) is equivalent to the \(\phi^*\)-smoothness inequality for \(f^*\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional subgradient formulation using Fenchel-conjugate moduli.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The curvature condition
\[
f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle s,y-x\rangle+\phi(\|y-x\|)
\quad\text{for all }x,y\in X\text{ and }s\in\partial f(x)
\]
is equivalent, under the stated hypotheses, to differentiability of \(f^*\) on \(X^*\) together with
\[
f^*(v)\le f^*(u)+\langle\nabla f^*(u),v-u\rangle
+\phi^*(\|v-u\|_*)
\quad\text{for all }u,v\in X^*.
\]
Thus primal curvature and dual smoothness exchange conjugate moduli.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform curvature controlled by phi corresponds under Fenchel conjugacy to dual smoothness controlled by the scalar conjugate phi-star.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modulus-paired uniform convexity and dual smoothness
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a real Banach space with dual \(X^*\), let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(f^*(u)=\sup_{x\in X}\{\langle u,x\rangle-f(x)\}\). Let \(\phi:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty]\) be convex with \(\phi(0)=0\), and define \(\phi^*(s)=\sup_{t\geq0}\{st-\phi(t)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition records a norm-dependent Banach-space correspondence using first-order remainder inequalities. It does not assert that every modulus yields the displayed dual relation without additional regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((f,f^*)\) has the uniform-convexity–dual-smoothness correspondence with primal modulus \(\phi\) when, for every \(x,y\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) and every \(u\in\partial f(x)\), \[f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle u,y-x\rangle+\phi(\|y-x\|),\] and, dually, for every \(u,v\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f^*\) and every \(x\in\partial f^*(u)\), \[f^*(v)\leq f^*(u)+\langle v-u,x\rangle+\phi^*(\|v-u\|_*).\] The first inequality defines uniform convexity through a subgradient remainder; the second defines the matched uniform smoothness of the conjugate through the scalar conjugate modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed convex function and its Fenchel conjugate form a modulus-paired uniformly convex and dually smooth pair when every primal subgradient model underestimates the function by at least \(\phi(\|y-x\|)\), while every dual subgradient model overestimates the conjugate by at most \(\phi^*(\|v-u\|_*)\). The norm and dual norm are part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f(y)-f(x)-\langle u,y-x\rangle\geq\phi(\|y-x\|),\qquad f^*(v)-f^*(u)-\langle v-u,x\rangle\leq\phi^*(\|v-u\|_*).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using the Bregman remainder \(D_f^u(y,x)=f(y)-f(x)-\langle u,y-x\rangle\), the primal condition is \(D_f^u(y,x)\geq\phi(\|y-x\|)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\phi(t)=\frac{\mu}{2}t^2\), the primal condition is \(\mu\)-strong convexity; its classical dual counterpart is differentiability of \(f^*\) with \((1/\mu)\)-Lipschitz gradient under the usual closedness and full-domain hypotheses.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\phi(t)>0\) for every \(t>0\), the primal inequality implies strict convexity on every convex subset of \(\operatorname{dom}\partial f\).
boundary_notes: The numerical modulus changes with the chosen norm.
The displayed generalized dual modulus requires an exact supporting source; the available source material only separately supports uniform convexity and quadratic strong-convexity duality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative smoothness and relative strong convexity pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(h:Q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and put \(U=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\cap Q\). Assume \(h\) and \(f:Q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are differentiable on \(U\). Define \(D_h(y,x)=h(y)-h(x)-\langle\nabla h(x),y-x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional differentiable relative curvature on a specified comparison set. Nonsmooth reference geometries require subgradient-based variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constants \(0\leq\mu\leq L<+\infty\), the pair \((f,h)\) is \((\mu,L)\)-relatively curved on \(U\) if, for all \(x,y\in U\), \[\mu D_h(y,x)\leq f(y)-f(x)-\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\leq L D_h(y,x).\] The upper inequality defines \(L\)-relative smoothness of \(f\) with respect to \(h\), and the lower inequality defines \(\mu\)-relative strong convexity. The ordered data \((f,h,Q,\mu,L)\), rather than \(f\) alone, constitutes the relative curvature class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective-reference pair \((f,h)\) has relative curvature parameters \((\mu,L)\) when the first-order remainder of \(f\) lies between \(\mu\) and \(L\) times the Bregman divergence generated by \(h\), for every ordered pair of points in the declared domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x,y\in U:\quad \mu D_h(y,x)\leq D_f(y,x)\leq L D_h(y,x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(f\) and \(h\) are differentiable convex functions on an open convex set, the condition is equivalent to convexity of \(f-\mu h\) and \(Lh-f\) on that set.

If both functions are twice differentiable, the condition is equivalently \(\mu
abla^2h(x)\preceq
abla^2f(x)\preceq L
abla^2h(x)\) for every \(x\in U\).
special_cases_latex: For \(h(x)=\frac12\|x\|_2^2\), the definition reduces to ordinary \(L\)-smoothness and \(\mu\)-strong convexity.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\mu>0\) and \(h\) is strictly convex, then \(f\) is strictly convex on \(U\).
boundary_notes: The constants are meaningful only relative to the chosen generator and comparison domain.
Boundary points at which the gradients do not exist are excluded.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex, let \(f,h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and differentiable, and let \(L\ge0\). The function \(f\) is \(L\)-smooth relative to \(h\) when \(Lh-f\) is convex on \(C\). Equivalently, for all \(x,y\in C\), \[D_f(y,x)\le LD_h(y,x),\] or \[f(y)\le f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+LD_h(y,x).\]

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and let \(f,h\) be differentiable on a convex set \(U\subseteq Q\cap\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\). For distinct \(x,y\in U\) with \(D_h(y,x)>0\), define \(R_{f|h}(y,x)=D_f(y,x)/D_h(y,x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition isolates dependence on both the reference generator and the set on which curvature comparisons are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The reference-geometry curvature interval of \(f\) relative to \(h\) on \(U\) is \[\mu_U(f|h)=\inf_{\substack{x,y\in U\,,\ x\ne y\\D_h(y,x)>0}}R_{f|h}(y,x),\qquad L_U(f|h)=\sup_{\substack{x,y\in U\,,\ x\ne y\\D_h(y,x)>0}}R_{f|h}(y,x).\] Reference-geometry dependence means that membership in a relative curvature class is assigned to the triple \((f,h,U)\): changing \(h\), its effective domain, or \(U\) may change either endpoint or make an endpoint infinite. Pairs satisfying \(D_h(y,x)=0\) are handled separately and require \(D_f(y,x)=0\) for a finite upper relative-smoothness constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative curvature is not an intrinsic property of the objective alone. Its best lower and upper constants are the infimum and supremum of the ratio between the Bregman remainders of the objective and reference function over the declared ordered pairs and domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mu_U(f|h)\,D_h(y,x)\leq D_f(y,x)\leq L_U(f|h)\,D_h(y,x)\quad(x,y\in U)\] whenever the zero-denominator compatibility condition holds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For finite constants, \(\mu_U(f|h)\) is the largest \(\mu\) for which \(f-\mu h\) is convex on \(U\), while \(L_U(f|h)\) is the smallest \(L\) for which \(Lh-f\) is convex on \(U\).
special_cases_latex: Replacing \(h\) by \(ah+b+\langle c,\cdot\rangle\) with \(a>0\) rescales both constants by \(1/a\), because affine terms do not change Bregman divergences.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(U_1\subseteq U_2\), then \(\mu_{U_1}(f|h)\geq\mu_{U_2}(f|h)\) and \(L_{U_1}(f|h)\leq L_{U_2}(f|h)\).

Constants computed on an open interior do not automatically extend to the boundary.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Self-concordant function and local Hessian geometry
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex with nonempty interior and let \(f:\operatorname{int}C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and three times continuously differentiable. For \(x\in\operatorname{int}C\), define the local seminorm \(\|h\|_x=(h^\top\nabla^2f(x)h)^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional classical self-concordance. The definition is a function-class interface; barrier parameters and path-following complexity are separate refinements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(f\) is self-concordant with constant \(M\geq0\) if, for every \(x\in\operatorname{int}C\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[|
abla^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\leq M\|h\|_x^3.\] It is standard self-concordant when \(M=2\). If \(
abla^2f(x)\succ0\), the associated dual local norm is \(\|u\|_{x,*}=(u^	op[
abla^2f(x)]^{-1}u)^{1/2}\), and the Newton decrement is \(\lambda_f(x)=\|
abla f(x)\|_{x,*}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-times continuously differentiable convex function is self-concordant when its third directional derivative is uniformly controlled by the three-halves power of its Hessian quadratic form. Constant two gives the standard normalization. The Hessian defines the local primal and dual norms used by Newton methods.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in\operatorname{int}C\ \forall h\in\mathbb{R}^n:\quad |\nabla^3f(x)[h,h,h]|\leq M(h^\top\nabla^2f(x)h)^{3/2}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because replacing \(h\) by \(-h\) reverses the sign of the trilinear value, the source's one-sided inequality is equivalent to the absolute-value form.
special_cases_latex: The function \(f(t)=-\log t\) on \((0,+\infty)\) is standard self-concordant.
immediate_consequences_latex: Where the Hessian is positive definite, self-concordance supplies an intrinsic local metric and the Newton decrement \(\lambda_f(x)\).
boundary_notes: Self-concordance alone is not the definition of a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier.
A singular Hessian yields only a seminorm unless an appropriate affine hull is used.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper with finite attained minimum \(f_*\), and let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\). Define \(G(x)=f(x)-f_*\), \(D(x)=d(x,S)\), and let \(R:X\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfy \(R^{-1}(0)=S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract function-level certificate system. Particular residuals may be subgradient, proximal-gradient, KKT, or feasibility residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A growth certificate system on a set \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) is the data \((G,D,R;\omega,\eta,\theta)\), where \(\omega,\eta,\theta:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty]\) vanish at zero, are positive on positive arguments in their stated ranges, and satisfy, for every \(x\in U\), \[G(x)\geq\omega(D(x)),\qquad D(x)\leq\eta(R(x)),\qquad G(x)\leq\theta(R(x)).\] Any nonempty subset of these inequalities is a partial certificate system, but its components and domain must be declared explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A growth certificate system relates three quantities: objective gap, distance to the solution set, and a residual whose zero set equals the solutions. Comparison functions specify which quantities bound the others on a declared region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad \omega(d(x,S))\leq f(x)-f_*\leq\theta(R(x)),\qquad d(x,S)\leq\eta(R(x)).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(\omega\) is strictly increasing, the growth inequality is equivalently \(D(x)\leq\omega^{-1}(G(x))\), using the generalized inverse.
special_cases_latex: Power comparison functions \(\omega(t)=ct^p\) produce exponent-parameterized objective growth.
Choosing \(R(x)=G(x)\) yields an objective-gap error bound.
immediate_consequences_latex: Composing valid comparison functions converts one certificate into another whenever the required inequalities have compatible directions.
boundary_notes: The zero-set condition alone does not imply any quantitative error bound.
All constants and comparison functions may be local or level-set dependent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective growth relative to the minimizer set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) attain its finite minimum \(f_*\), and let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\). Let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) contain \(S\), and let \(\omega:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfy \(\omega(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General, possibly local, growth condition relative to a non-singleton solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has \(\omega\)-objective growth on \(U\) if \[f(x)-f_*\geq\omega(d(x,S))\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] The condition is strict when \(\omega(t)>0\) for every positive distance attained on \(U\). A constant-modulus power growth condition is obtained by taking \(\omega(t)=ct^p\) with \(c>0\) and \(p>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective growth means that the objective gap is bounded below by a prescribed function of the distance from the point to the entire minimizer set. The domain on which the inequality is required is part of the condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad f(x)-\inf f\geq\omega\bigl(d(x,\operatorname{argmin}f)\bigr).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\omega\) is strictly increasing, the condition is equivalently \(d(x,S)\leq\omega^{-1}(f(x)-f_*)\) on \(U\), with generalized inverse if necessary.
special_cases_latex: The choices \(\omega(t)=\alpha t\) and \(\omega(t)=\frac\mu2t^2\) give sharp and quadratic growth, respectively.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\omega(t)>0\) for \(t>0\), every point in \(U\) having zero objective gap belongs to \(S\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Growth Does Not Imply Strong Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the converse from quadratic growth to strong convexity or uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1^2\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), the minimizer set is \(S=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\) and \[f(x)-\min f=\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2.\] Thus \(f\) has global quadratic growth with \(\alpha=2\) under the convention \((\alpha/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\), but it is neither strictly nor strongly convex and has nonunique minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared distance to a line has exact quadratic growth but is flat along its minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f^*=\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\), while \(f\) is not strongly convex and \(S\) is not a singleton.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Growth Does Not Imply Strong Convexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Growth Implies a Subgradient Residual Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order residual consequence of quadratic growth for proper closed convex functions on a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f(x)-f^*\ge(\alpha/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\) on a region containing \(S\). Then every point \(x\) in that region and every \(g\in\partial f(x)\) satisfy \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\frac{2}{\alpha}\lVert g\rVert.\] Equivalently, \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le(2/\alpha)\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\) whenever the subdifferential is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex quadratic growth converts small subgradient residual into a quantitative distance bound to the solution set.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex on a Hilbert space.
Quadratic growth with modulus \(\alpha>0\) holds on the stated region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le(2/\alpha)\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\) at points with nonempty subdifferential.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic growth about a minimizer set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) have finite attained minimum \(f_*\), and let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\). Let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) contain \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued quadratic growth; global or local scope is determined by U.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) satisfies quadratic growth with modulus \(\mu>0\) on \(U\) if \[f(x)-f_*\geq\frac{\mu}{2}\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] The best quadratic-growth modulus on \(U\) is \[\mu_U^{\mathrm{qg}}=\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}\frac{2(f(x)-f_*)}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2},\] with the convention that the infimum is \(+\infty\) when \(U\setminus S\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth requires the objective gap to dominate one half of a positive constant times the squared distance to the full solution set. The best modulus is the infimum of the resulting gap-to-squared-distance ratio.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad f(x)\geq f_*+\frac\mu2\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inequality is equivalently the objective-gap error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\sqrt{2(f(x)-f_*)/\mu}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(S=\{x_*\}\), the right-hand side becomes \(f_*+\frac\mu2\|x-x_*\|^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Quadratic growth makes every sufficiently small objective gap quantitatively control distance to the solution set.
boundary_notes: Quadratic growth is weaker than strong convexity because it compares only with the minimizer set.
The factor \(1/2\) is a normalization convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Power-type objective growth of order p
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) attain its finite minimum \(f_*\), let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\), and let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) contain \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponent-parameterized growth relative to a possibly non-singleton solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p>0\) and \(c>0\), the function \(f\) has power-type growth of order \(p\) with constant \(c\) on \(U\) if \[f(x)-f_*\geq c\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p\qquad(x\in U).\] Its best order-\(p\) constant is \[c_{p,U}=\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}\frac{f(x)-f_*}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p}.\] The exponent, constant, norm, solution set, and localization set are all part of the declared growth class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power growth of order \(p\) means that the objective gap dominates a positive constant times the \(p\)-th power of distance to the minimizer set throughout a specified region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad f(x)-f_*\geq c\,\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition is equivalently \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq c^{-1/p}(f(x)-f_*)^{1/p}\) on \(U\).
special_cases_latex: Order \(p=1\) is sharp growth.
Order \(p=2\) is quadratic growth, with \(c=\mu/2\) under the common quadratic normalization.
immediate_consequences_latex: An objective accuracy \(f(x)-f_*\leq\varepsilon\) implies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq(\varepsilon/c)^{1/p}\).
boundary_notes: Comparisons between different exponents depend on whether distances are below or above one.
Exponents below one may be incompatible with common convex interior geometries and therefore require explicit scope.

children.title: Growth Exponent Regimes
children.top_down_role: Qualitative regimes arising from different growth exponents.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sublinear Exponents Are Excluded at Accessible Isolated Convex Minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex lower boundary for growth exponents; isolated-domain degeneracies are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex on a normed space. Suppose \(\bar x\) is an isolated minimizer and \(\operatorname{dom}f\) contains a point distinct from \(\bar x\). For every \(0<p<1\), there are no \(\kappa,\varepsilon>0\) such that \[f(x)-f(\bar x)\geq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname*{argmin}f)^p\] for all \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nontrivially accessible isolated minimizer of a convex function, local power growth cannot have exponent below one.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}f\) contains a point distinct from \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No local bound \(f-f^*\geq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S)^p\) with \(\kappa>0\) can hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Sublinear Exponents Are Excluded at Accessible Isolated Convex Minima

assumptions_latex: \(X^*\neq\varnothing\), and \(0<\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\leq r\) on the local comparison region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_1\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^{p_1}\geq\kappa_1r^{p_1-p_2}\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)^{p_2}\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local ordering and interpretation of power-growth exponents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the region \(d(x)\leq r\), exponents are ordered by \[ d(x)^{p_1}\geq r^{p_1-p_2}d(x)^{p_2}\qquad(0<p_1<p_2). \] Hence power growth of the smaller order \(p_1\) implies local power growth of every larger order \(p_2\), after rescaling the modulus. Near \(X^*\), smaller exponents therefore express stronger growth. This ordering is only local: for \(d(x)>1\), the ordering of powers reverses, so exponent comparison alone does not yield a global implication on an unbounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near the solution set, smaller growth exponents are stronger and imply larger exponents; on unbounded domains, powers reverse order at large distances.
knowledge_statements.title: Growth Exponent Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local ordering of powers is correct and appropriately recorded as a property, but the claimed regime interpretation lacks cited evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sublinear Growth Exponents Are Excluded at Accessible Isolated Convex Minima

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex on a normed space, let \(\bar x\) be an isolated minimizer, and suppose there exists \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f\setminus\{\bar x\}\). Then no constants \(\kappa,\\varepsilon>0\) and exponent \(0<p<1\) can satisfy \[ f(x)-f(\bar x)\geq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname*{argmin}f)^p \] for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\). Indeed, along \(x_t=(1-t)\bar x+ty\), convexity makes the objective gap at most linear in \(t\), whereas isolation makes the distance to the solution set proportional to \(t\); for \(p<1\), the proposed lower bound is asymptotically larger than linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nontrivially accessible isolated minimizer of a convex function, local power growth cannot have exponent below one.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}f\) contains a point distinct from \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No local lower bound \(f-f^*\geq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S)^p\) with \(\kappa>0\) can hold.

children.title: Growth Localization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood-restricted versus domain-wide growth behavior.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) attain its finite minimum \(f_*\) on a metric space \((X,d)\), let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\), and let \(\omega:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty]\) vanish at zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition distinguishes only the quantification region; it does not change the growth modulus itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The growth inequality \(f(x)-f_*\geq\omega(d(x,S))\) is global if it holds for all \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\). It is neighborhood-local if there exists \(r>0\) such that it holds whenever \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(d(x,S)<r\). It is level-set-local if there exists \(\delta>0\) such that it holds whenever \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(f(x)\leq f_*+\delta\). The constants \(r\) or \(\delta\) belong to the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A growth condition is global when quantified over the entire effective domain, neighborhood-local when restricted to a metric tube around the solution set, and level-set-local when restricted to a sufficiently low objective sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\begin{aligned}\text{global: }&x\in\operatorname{dom}f,\\\text{neighborhood-local: }&d(x,S)<r,\\\text{level-set-local: }&f(x)-f_*\leq\delta,
\end{aligned}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f(x)-f_*\geq\omega(d(x,S)).\]
special_cases_latex: For \(\omega(t)=ct^p\), these regimes give global, local, and sublevel-local power growth.
immediate_consequences_latex: A global certificate is automatically valid in every neighborhood and sublevel restriction.
A level-set-local certificate controls all sufficiently accurate objective approximations.
boundary_notes: Neighborhood-local and level-set-local regimes need not coincide without continuity or compactness assumptions.
The localization radius may be uniform around the whole solution set or pointwise; this record uses the uniform setwise version.
review_flags: No inspected source stated this three-way localization taxonomy with the same uniform conventions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Local Quadratic Growth Without Global Quadratic Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth convex separation of local and global quadratic-growth regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\sqrt{1+x^2}-1\) on \(\mathbb R\), \(\operatorname*{argmin}f=\{0\}\) and, when \(|x|\le1\), \[f(x)=\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1+x^2}+1}\ge\frac{x^2}{\sqrt2+1}.\] Hence local quadratic growth holds. However, \(\lim_{|x|\to\infty}f(x)/x^2=0\), so no positive global quadratic-growth modulus exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The function square-root of one plus x squared, minus one, is locally quadratic at its minimizer but only linear at infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local quadratic growth holds at \(0\), but \(\inf_{x\ne0}f(x)/x^2=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Local Quadratic Growth Without Global Quadratic Growth

assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) has minimum value \(f^*\) and nonempty minimizer set \(S\).
\(U\subset X\) is a neighborhood of \(S\), and \(\omega(t)>0\) for \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localization gap occurs when the growth inequality holds on \(U\) but \(\inf_{x\notin U}(f(x)-f^*)/\omega(\operatorname{dist}(x,S))=0\).

notation.meaning: neighborhood on which growth is certified

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes neighborhood growth from a uniform global certificate.

source_refs.locator: 10 Convex Functions: Variants p. 177
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed growth function \(\omega\), a localization gap is present when
\[
f(x)-f^*\geq \omega\!\left(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\right)
\quad\text{for every }x\in U\cap\operatorname{dom}f,
\]
but no positive uniform multiple of the same growth function works globally, equivalently
\[
\inf_{x\in\operatorname{dom}f\setminus U}
\frac{f(x)-f^*}{\omega(\operatorname{dist}(x,S))}=0,
\]
where the quotient is considered only at points outside \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A localization gap exists when a growth bound holds near the solution set but every global bound of the same form has zero modulus.
knowledge_statements.title: Localization Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak sharpness of a minimizer set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a normed space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) have finite attained minimum \(f_*\), let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\), and let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) contain \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order, set-valued sharp growth; uniqueness is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The solution set \(S\) is weakly sharp for \(f\) on \(U\) with modulus \(\alpha>0\) if \[f(x)-f_*\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] The best sharpness modulus is \[\alpha_U=\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}\frac{f(x)-f_*}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)}.\] When \(S=\{x_*\}\), this is isolated sharpness of \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak sharpness is linear objective growth away from the minimizer set. It permits multiple minimizers and measures transverse separation from the entire solution set rather than from a selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad f(x)\geq f_*+\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inequality is equivalently the Lipschitz objective-gap error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq(f(x)-f_*)/\alpha\).
special_cases_latex: For a singleton solution set, \(f(x)-f(x_*)\geq\alpha\|x-x_*\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every point with objective gap at most \(\varepsilon\) lies within distance \(\varepsilon/\alpha\) of \(S\).
boundary_notes: Weak sharpness does not mean differentiability or strong convexity.
The adjective weak refers to allowing a non-singleton solution set, not to a smaller positive modulus.
review_flags: No precise source locator for weak sharp minima was found in the inspected corpus.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak sharpness of a minimizer set

children.title: Weak Sharp Minima
children.top_down_role: Set-relative sharpness allowing nonunique minimizers.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space, \(D\subseteq X\) contains \(S\), and \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is a set of weak sharp minima of \(f\) with modulus \(\alpha\) on \(D\) exactly when \(f(x)-f^*\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\) for every \(x\in D\cap\operatorname{dom}f\).

notation.meaning: region on which weak sharpness is asserted

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-relative linear growth; the minimizer set need not be a singleton.

source_refs.locator: 10 Convex Functions: Variants p. 177
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The minimizer set \(S\) is a set of weak sharp minima of \(f\) with modulus \(\alpha>0\) on a set \(D\supseteq S\) if
\[
f(x)-f^*\geq \alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)
\quad\text{for every }x\in D\cap\operatorname{dom}f.
\]
The property is global when \(D=X\), and local when \(D\) is a neighborhood of \(S\). The definition permits multiple minimizers and measures sharpness relative to the entire set \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak sharpness means that the objective gap grows at least linearly with distance to the possibly non-singleton minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Sharp Minima

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Growth Is Not Weak Sharpness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical failure of local and global linear growth for a smooth convex minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), \(S=\{0\}\), but
\[
\inf_{x\ne0}\frac{f(x)-\min f}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)}
=\inf_{x\ne0}|x|=0.
\]
Moreover, the same infimum is zero after restriction to any neighborhood of zero. Thus no \(\alpha>0\) gives local or global weak sharpness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic minimum is not weakly sharp because its objective gap is second order rather than linear near the solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maximal local and global weak-sharpness moduli at \(S=\{0\}\) are zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Growth Is Not Weak Sharpness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best modulus on a fixed region, encompassing the global case and any specified local region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\), let \(f^*=\min f\), and let \(D\supseteq S\). Then
\[
\alpha_D:=\sup\{\alpha\geq0:f(x)-f^*\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\ \forall x\in D\cap\operatorname{dom}f\}
=\inf_{x\in(D\cap\operatorname{dom}f)\setminus S}
\frac{f(x)-f^*}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)},
\]
where the infimum of the empty set is \(+\infty\). Weak sharpness on \(D\) holds with a positive modulus exactly when \(\alpha_D>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On any fixed region, the best weak-sharpness constant is the infimum of objective gap divided by distance to the minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_D=\inf_{x\in(D\cap\operatorname{dom}f)\setminus S}(f(x)-f^*)/\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\), and positive weak sharpness on \(D\) is equivalent to \(\alpha_D>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Regional Weak-Sharpness Modulus

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximal global modulus expressed as the minimum normalized objective growth away from the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper with nonempty minimizer set \(S\) and minimum \(f^*\). The maximal global weak-sharpness modulus is
\[
\alpha_*:=\sup\{\alpha\geq0:f(x)-f^*\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\ \forall x\}
=\inf_{x\in\operatorname{dom}f\setminus S}
\frac{f(x)-f^*}{\operatorname{dist}(x,S)},
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). Positive global weak sharpness holds exactly when \(\alpha_*>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best weak-sharpness constant is the infimum of the objective gap divided by distance to the minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_*=\inf_{x\in\operatorname{dom}f\setminus S}(f(x)-f^*)/\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\), and weak sharpness holds with a positive modulus exactly when \(\alpha_*>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Weak-Sharpness Modulus

children.title: Isolated Sharp Minima
children.top_down_role: Sharpness centered on isolated solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a normed space, and \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is an isolated sharp minimizer when \(f(x)-f(\bar x)\geq\alpha\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) satisfying \(\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local linear growth centered at one solution.

source_refs.locator: 10 Convex Functions: Variants p. 177
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A point \(\bar x\) is an isolated sharp minimizer of \(f\) if there exist \(\alpha>0\) and \(r>0\) such that
\[
f(x)-f(\bar x)\geq \alpha\lVert x-\bar x\rVert
\quad\text{whenever }x\in\operatorname{dom}f
\text{ and }\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<r.
\]
This inequality implies that \(\bar x\) is the unique minimizer in the open ball of radius \(r\), although other minimizers may exist outside that ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An isolated sharp minimizer has a local linear objective increase in every direction away from that single solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Isolated Sharp Minima

source_witnesses.locator: 10 Convex Functions: Variants p. 177

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global consequence of a locally isolated sharp minimum under convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be convex on a normed space. If \[f(x)-f(\bar x)\ge\alpha\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\] for every domain point satisfying \(\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<r\), where \(\alpha,r>0\), then the same inequality holds for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\). Consequently, \(\operatorname*{argmin}f=\{\bar x\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective, locally isolated sharpness extends globally and forces a unique global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a normed space.
The centered sharp-growth inequality holds on some ball about \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f(\bar x)\ge\alpha\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\) globally and \(\operatorname*{argmin}f=\{\bar x\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Local Sharpness Globalizes

children.title: Subdifferential Sharpness Certificates
children.top_down_role: First-order certificate families associated with sharp minimizer geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional directional characterization of global weak sharpness for a convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\). For \(\alpha>0\),
\[
f(x)-\min f\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\quad(\forall x)
\]
holds if and only if
\[
f'(s;d)\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(d,T_S(s))
\quad(\forall s\in S,\ d\in\mathbb R^n).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global weak sharpness is equivalent to each directional derivative at a minimizer dominating the direction's distance from the tangent cone.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-\min f\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S)\) globally if and only if \(f'(s;d)\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(d,T_S(s))\) for all \(s\in S\) and \(d\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: one-sided directional derivative of f at s in direction d
tangent cone to S at s

knowledge_statements.title: Directional-Derivative Sharpness Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary first-order residual separation outside the minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\), and suppose
\[
f(x)-\min f\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n
\]
for some \(\alpha>0\). Then every \(x\notin S\) and every \(g\in\partial f(x)\) satisfy
\[
\|g\|\geq\alpha.
\]
Consequently, if \(\partial f(x)\neq\varnothing\), then \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\geq\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under global weak sharpness, every subgradient outside the solution set has norm at least the sharpness modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\notin S\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\), \(\|g\|\geq\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient-Norm Consequence of Weak Sharpness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Centered-Ball Subdifferential Certificate for a Sharp Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional first-order certificate for global linear growth away from a single minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\), and let \(B\) be the closed Euclidean unit ball. For \(\alpha>0\),
\[
f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\alpha\|x-\bar x\|\quad(\forall x\in\mathbb R^n)
\]
holds if and only if
\[
\alpha B\subseteq\partial f(\bar x).
\]
Consequently, some positive modulus exists exactly when \(0\in\operatorname{int}\partial f(\bar x)\), and the largest admissible modulus is \(\sup\{r\ge0:rB\subseteq\partial f(\bar x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global linear growth from a minimizer is equivalent to its subdifferential containing a centered ball, whose inradius is the best sharpness modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(B\) is the closed Euclidean unit ball and \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\alpha\|x-\bar x\|\) for every \(x\) if and only if \(\alpha B\subseteq\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Centered-Ball Subdifferential Certificate for a Sharp Minimizer

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\), and \(B\) is the closed Euclidean unit ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global weak sharpness with modulus \(\alpha\) is equivalent to \(\alpha(B\cap N_S(s))\subseteq\partial f(s)\) for every \(s\in S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex certificate for global weak sharpness.

source_refs.locator: 9.2 Proper Lower Semicontinuous Convex Functions p. 160
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha>0\), the global weak-sharpness inequality
\[
f(x)-\min f\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)
\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n
\]
is equivalent to the pointwise first-order inclusions
\[
\alpha\bigl(B\cap N_S(s)\bigr)\subseteq\partial f(s)
\quad\text{for every }s\in S.
\]
Thus each unit normal direction to the solution set, scaled by \(\alpha\), must be supported by a subgradient at the corresponding minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak sharpness is certified when every scaled unit normal to the solution set is a subgradient at the corresponding minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential Sharpness Certificates

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\). Let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) contain \(S\), and define \(r_{\partial f}(x)=\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex subdifferential residual certificate away from the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has a subdifferential sharpness certificate with modulus \(\alpha>0\) on \(U\) if \[\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x))\geq\alpha\qquad\text{for every }x\in U\setminus S.\] Its certificate modulus is \[\alpha_{\partial,U}=\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x)).\] At solution points, convex optimality gives \(0\in\partial f(x)\), so the certificate is intentionally imposed only off \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subdifferential sharpness certificate is a uniform positive lower bound on the smallest dual norm of a subgradient at every nonsolution point in the declared region. At minimizers the residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in U\setminus S\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \inf_{v\in\partial f(x)}\|v\|_*\geq\alpha.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition is \(\inf_{x\in U\setminus S}r_{\partial f}(x)>0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f\) is differentiable away from \(S\), the residual becomes \(\|\nabla f(x)\|_*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The certificate rules out sequences of nonsolution points in \(U\) whose minimal subgradient norms converge to zero.
boundary_notes: For merely local sharpness, U must be restricted accordingly.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) is polyhedral convex and attains its minimum, then its minimizer set \(S\) is polyhedral and there exists a constant \(\alpha>0\) such that
\[
f(x)-\min f\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)
\quad\text{for every }x\in\operatorname{dom}f.
\]
Hence the finitely many affine pieces defining the epigraph induce a uniform global linear-growth modulus relative to the entire solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every proper polyhedral convex objective that attains its minimum has a global linear growth bound relative to its minimizer set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual error bound for a solution set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space, let \(S\subseteq X\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(R:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a residual satisfying \(R(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\in S\). Let \(U\subseteq X\) contain \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract error-bound definition encompassing objective, stationarity, composite, and feasibility residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The residual \(R\) provides an error bound for \(S\) on \(U\) with modulus \(\eta:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty]\) if \(\eta(0)=0\) and \[d(x,S)\leq\eta(R(x))\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] A linear error bound has \(\eta(t)=\kappa t\) for some \(\kappa>0\), while a Hölder error bound has \(\eta(t)=\kappa t^\theta\) with \(\theta\in(0,1]\). The residual, solution set, region, and modulus are all part of the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An error bound controls distance to the solution set by a specified function of a computable or analytic residual whose zero set is exactly the solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad d(x,S)\leq\eta(R(x)),\qquad R^{-1}(0)=S.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\eta\) is strictly increasing, the inequality is equivalently \(R(x)\geq\eta^{-1}(d(x,S))\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(R(x)=f(x)-f_*\) gives an objective-gap error bound.
For convex optimization, taking \(R(x)=\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x))\) gives a subgradient-residual error bound.
immediate_consequences_latex: A sequence in \(U\) with \(R(x_k)\to0\) satisfies \(d(x_k,S)\to0\) whenever \(\eta(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
boundary_notes: Residual consistency \(R^{-1}(0)=S\) does not itself imply an error bound.
Local and global error bounds must be distinguished through U.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An objective-gap error bound with exponent \(\theta>0\) and constant \(c>0\) holds on \(D\) if
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)
\leq c\bigl(f(x)-f^*\bigr)^\theta
\quad\text{for every }x\in D\cap\operatorname{dom}f.
\]
It is global when \(D=X\) and local when \(D\) is a neighborhood or sublevel set containing \(S\). For \(\theta=1\), this is equivalent to linear objective growth with modulus \(1/c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective-gap error bound controls distance to the solution set by a power of the objective suboptimality.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space and let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) attain its finite minimum \(f_*\). Set \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\), and let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) contain \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value residual error bound relative to the complete minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) satisfies an objective-gap error bound on \(U\) with modulus \(\eta:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty]\), where \(\eta(0)=0\), if \[d(x,S)\leq\eta(f(x)-f_*)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] A Hölder objective-gap error bound has \(\eta(t)=\kappa t^\theta\) for constants \(\kappa>0\) and \(\theta>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective-gap error bound uses the nonnegative value difference \(f(x)-f_*\) as the residual and bounds the distance from \(x\) to the entire minimizer set by a prescribed modulus of that gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad d(x,\operatorname{argmin}f)\leq\eta(f(x)-\inf f).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\eta(t)=\kappa t^\theta\), the bound is equivalently \(f(x)-f_*\geq\kappa^{-1/\theta}d(x,S)^{1/\theta}\).
special_cases_latex: Quadratic growth with modulus \(\mu\) gives \(\eta(t)=\sqrt{2t/\mu}\).
Sharp growth with modulus \(\alpha\) gives \(\eta(t)=t/\alpha\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Vanishing objective gaps force convergence in distance to \(S\) whenever \(\eta(t)\to0\) at zero.
boundary_notes: The bound does not identify which minimizer is approached when S is non-singleton.
Knowledge of \(f_*\) may be unavailable computationally even though the error bound is analytically valid.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\) for every \(x\in D\), with \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\varnothing)=+\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A subgradient-residual error bound holds on \(D\) with constant \(\kappa>0\) when
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)
\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial f(x)\bigr)
\quad\text{for every }x\in D.
\]
Here \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\varnothing)=+\infty\). The residual vanishes exactly at minimizers because convex optimality gives \(0\in\partial f(x)\) if and only if \(x\in S\). Restricting \(D\) yields a local error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient-residual error bound controls solution distance by the norm of a smallest subgradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient-Residual Error Bounds

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional normed space and let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \(S=\operatorname{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\). Let \(U\subseteq\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) contain \(S\), and define \(R_{\partial}(x)=\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex subdifferential residual; finite dimensionality avoids additional weak-topology qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) satisfies a subgradient-residual error bound on \(U\) with modulus \(\eta:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty]\), where \(\eta(0)=0\), if \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\eta\bigl(\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x))\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] A linear subgradient error bound has \(\eta(t)=\kappa t\); equivalently, \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}_*(0,\partial f(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient-residual error bound controls distance to the minimizer set by the smallest dual norm among all convex subgradients at the point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in U:\quad \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\eta\left(\inf_{v\in\partial f(x)}\|v\|_*\right).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The linear form is metric subregularity of the convex subdifferential at residual value zero, uniformly over the specified portion of its zero set.
special_cases_latex: If \(f\) is differentiable on \(U\), then \(R_{\partial}(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|_*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(R_{\partial}(x_k)\to0\) and \(\eta(t)\to0\) at zero, then \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\to0\).
boundary_notes: Points outside \(\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) are excluded.
For nonconvex functions, the chosen generalized subdifferential must be specified and the zero set may include nonoptimal stationary points.

notation.meaning: distance measured in the dual norm

children.title: Composite Residual Certificate Family
children.top_down_role: Residual families adapted to composite optimization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(F=f+g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), where \(f\) is convex and differentiable on an open set containing \(\operatorname{dom}g\), and let \(g\) be proper, closed, and convex. Write \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}F\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex composite minimization; the definition is local on a specified set and allows any residual map whose zeros coincide locally with minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \(\{R_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\), with \(R_\lambda:\Omega\to X\), is a composite residual certificate family for \(F=f+g\) on \(U\subseteq\Omega\) if, for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), \(R_\lambda(x)=0\iff x\in S\) for \(x\in U\), and there are \(\kappa_\lambda>0\) and \(q_\lambda>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq \kappa_\lambda\|R_\lambda(x)\|^{q_\lambda}\qquad(x\in U).\] A canonical proximal-gradient member is \(R_\gamma(x)=\gamma^{-1}\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x-\gamma\nabla f(x))\bigr)\), \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite residual certificate family consists of residual maps whose zeros are exactly the composite minimizers on the stated region and whose magnitudes quantitatively control distance to the solution set. For the proximal-gradient residual, the residual is the scaled difference between the current point and its forward-backward update.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable on a neighborhood of \(\operatorname{dom}g\).
\(g\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}(f+g)\neq\varnothing\).
\(U\subseteq\Omega\) is the region on which the zero-set identity and error bound are asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\lambda^{-1}(0)\cap U=S\cap U\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa_\lambda\|R_\lambda(x)\|^{q_\lambda}\) for every \(x\in U\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(q_\lambda=1\), the certificate is the metric-subregularity inequality \(\operatorname{dist}(x,R_\lambda^{-1}(0))\leq\kappa_\lambda\operatorname{dist}(0,R_\lambda(x))\) on \(U\).
special_cases_latex: If \(g=0\), then \(R_\gamma=\nabla f\).
If \(f=0\), then \(R_\gamma(x)=\gamma^{-1}(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any sequence \(x_k\in U\) satisfying \(\|R_\lambda(x_k)\|\to0\) also satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\to0\).
boundary_notes: The zero-set identity alone is only a stationarity certificate and does not provide an error bound.
The constants and exponent may be local and may depend on the residual parameter.

notation.meaning: solution set of the composite problem

review_flags: No inspected source in the supplied locator set states this residual-family definition with the exact zero-set and Hölder error-bound clauses.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite residual error-bound certificate

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\lVert x-T_t(x)\rVert\) for every \(x\in D\).

source_refs.locator: 10.4 Analysis of the Proximal Gradient Method-The Convex Case p. 281

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proximal residual bound with constant \(\kappa>0\) holds on \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) if
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)
\leq\kappa\left\lVert x-T_t(x)\right\rVert
\quad\text{for every }x\in D.
\]
The residual is directly computable from one forward-backward step. Moreover, \(x=T_t(x)\) is equivalent to \(0\in\nabla g(x)+\partial h(x)\), hence to \(x\in S\) under the stated convex assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal residual bound controls distance to composite minimizers by the displacement produced by one proximal-gradient step.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Residual Bounds

children.title: Gradient-Mapping Bounds
children.top_down_role: Error bounds expressed through gradient-mapping residuals.

assumptions_latex: \(F=g+h\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), where \(g\) is differentiable and convex and \(h\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\lVert G_t(x)\rVert\) for every \(x\in D\).

notation.meaning: region on which the gradient-mapping bound is asserted

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled proximal-gradient residual error bound.

source_refs.locator: 10.4 Analysis of the Proximal Gradient Method-The Convex Case p. 281

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A gradient-mapping error bound with constant \(\kappa>0\) holds on \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) if
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)
\leq\kappa\lVert G_t(x)\rVert
\quad\text{for every }x\in D.
\]
The mapping \(G_t\) reduces to \(\nabla g\) when \(h=0\), and \(G_t(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) satisfies the composite first-order optimality condition \(0\in\nabla g(x)+\partial h(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gradient-mapping bound controls distance to composite solutions by the scaled proximal-gradient displacement.

children.title: Composite Residual Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Comparative geometry among residual certificates for composite models.

assumptions_latex: \(F=g+h\), where \(g\) is convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(h\) is proper lower-semicontinuous convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert x-x^+\rVert=t\lVert G_t(x)\rVert\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^+))\leq(1+Lt)\lVert G_t(x)\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of displacement, gradient-mapping, and post-step stationarity residuals.

source_refs.locator: 10.4 Analysis of the Proximal Gradient Method-The Convex Case p. 281

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The proximal displacement and gradient mapping satisfy the exact identity
\[
\lVert x-x^+\rVert=t\lVert G_t(x)\rVert.
\]
Proximal optimality also gives
\[
G_t(x)-\nabla g(x)+\nabla g(x^+)\in\partial F(x^+).
\]
Consequently, Lipschitz continuity of \(\nabla g\) yields
\[
\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial F(x^+)\bigr)
\leq(1+Lt)\lVert G_t(x)\rVert.
\]
Thus a gradient-mapping residual controls a subgradient residual at the computed proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal displacement equals the stepsize times the gradient mapping, which also bounds stationarity at the new proximal point.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Residual Comparisons

source_witnesses.locator: 10.4 Analysis of the Proximal Gradient Method-The Convex Case p. 281

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stationarity equivalence for the forward-backward fixed point and gradient mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t>0\), \[G_t(x)=0\iff x=\operatorname{prox}_{th}(x-t\nabla g(x))\iff 0\in\nabla g(x)+\partial h(x)=\partial F(x).\] If \(F\) is convex, these conditions are equivalent to \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero proximal displacement, zero gradient mapping, a forward-backward fixed point, composite stationarity, and convex optimality are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_t(x)=0\iff0\in\partial F(x)\iff x\in\operatorname*{argmin}F.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Composite Residual Equivalence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Current-Point Stationarity Dominates the Gradient Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison from a composite subgradient at the current point to the proximal-gradient residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{th}(x-t\nabla g(x))\) and \(G_t(x)=t^{-1}(x-x^+)\). For every \(v\in\partial h(x)\), \[\|G_t(x)\|\leq\|\nabla g(x)+v\|.\] Consequently, \[\|G_t(x)\|\leq\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-gradient mapping at x is no larger than the smallest composite subgradient residual at x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lVert G_t(x)\rVert\leq\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x)).
knowledge_statements.title: Current-Point Stationarity Dominates the Gradient Mapping

children.title: Feasibility Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Distance control through violations of constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility error bound for a constraint system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be metric spaces, let \(G:X\rightrightarrows Y\), fix \(\bar y\in Y\), and define the feasible set \(C=G^{-1}(\bar y)=\{x:\bar y\in G(x)\}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-space formulation, local or global according to the chosen region; Hölder and linear bounds are distinguished by the exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The system \(\bar y\in G(x)\) has a Hölder feasibility error bound of order \(q>0\) on \(U\subseteq X\) with constant \(\kappa>0\) if \[\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,G(x))^q\qquad\text{for every }x\in U,\] with \(\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,\varnothing)=+\infty\). It has a local error bound at \(\bar x\in C\) when this holds on some neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), and a global error bound when \(U=X\). The case \(q=1\) is a linear feasibility error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility error bound controls the distance from any tested point to the feasible set by a constant times a power of its constraint violation. It is local if asserted only near a feasible reference point and global if asserted throughout the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,G(x))^q\) for all \(x\in U\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(q=1\) and local \(U\), the inequality is metric subregularity of \(G\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
For scalar inequalities \(g_i(x)\leq0\), one may take \(G(x)=g(x)+\mathbb R_+^m\), giving residual \(\operatorname{dist}(g(x),-\mathbb R_+^m)\).
special_cases_latex: For an equation \(F(x)=0\), the bound becomes \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(0))\leq\kappa\|F(x)\|^q\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If the residual tends to zero along points in \(U\), their distances to \(C\) tend to zero.
boundary_notes: An error bound does not require uniqueness of a feasible point.
A local bound need not extend globally with one uniform constant.
